headline: Operational-expansion opportunities across 12 real mid-market & enterprise accounts
summary: A real-evidence validation of LeadLens temporal intelligence: 12 accounts evaluated against Asteron's operational-expansion thesis, each Case built only from dated, sourced public evidence. Four accounts show recent, independently corroborated expansion; four need validation; four have no current dated trigger.

allocation.line: Focus first on the four corroborated, recent expansions
allocation.detail: Saia, Watsco, Encompass Health and Alianza Team each show a dated, independently corroborated operational expansion aligned to Asteron's thesis.

portfolio.note: All 12 evaluated accounts remain visible regardless of evidence outcome.

accounts.decisionNote: Dated facility opening corroborated by independent trade (foodnavigator) + Colombian press (elnorte) — the strongest Colombian case.
accounts.thesis: A Colombian B2B fats/oils manufacturer expanding internationally — a plant build-out that adds cross-border operations and distribution complexity.
accounts.whyItMatters: A new US plant plus export growth introduces multi-country operations and distribution coordination — precisely where Asteron's orchestration reduces onboarding time; the plant is newly live.

accounts.decisionNote: Recent, material, independently corroborated network expansion aligned to Asteron's core profile.
accounts.thesis: A multi-terminal LTL carrier standing up new terminals month after month — a physical-network build-out that strains routing, dock and yard tooling.
accounts.whyItMatters: Each new terminal is a new operating node Asteron's TMS/orchestration must model; a rapid multi-site build-out is exactly when a carrier re-evaluates network tooling — the window is open now, not after the network settles.

whatChanged.event: Opened new LTL terminals across the Midwest (Duluth, Columbia, Marysville WA, Indiana) — a third consecutive month of terminal openings.

commercialContext.objective: Find enterprise accounts where operational expansion creates a credible near-term software opportunity.
commercialContext.clientDescription: Enterprise logistics & operations software (WMS/TMS/orchestration) for multi-site operators.
commercialContext.summary: The account is scaling physical operations — new distribution centers, terminals, plants, facilities, capacity, or acquisitions — which strains existing tooling and creates a near-term systems need.

items: Confirm whether the new plant has moved from plan to build (decision-critical).
Find independent corroboration + any newer DC activity (decision-critical).
Corroborate the Bison acquisition scope via primary sources (decision-critical).
Determine whether new-hub/automation growth outweighs the layoff/closure footprint (decision-critical).
Locate which region carries the net-new operations.

coverage.note: 8/12 accounts carry dated evidence; 7/12 independently corroborated.

methodology: Accounts selected first by structural criteria (sector, operational intensity, public visibility) — never because an event was known.
Evidence gated: identity → real event date → materiality → client-relevance → independent origin.
Retrieval/crawl dates, static pages and wrong-entity matches rejected.
Counterevidence gathered by a separate adversarial pass.
limitations: Spanish-language operational news has weaker public recall — several Colombian accounts may have events not surfaced in-window.
Some acquisitions are corroborated by secondary finance aggregators rather than primary filings.
